Life cycles

Source: R/model.R
life_cycles.Rd

  • wright_fisher() (the default): discrete generations. Every generation, each individual mutates and the whole population is replaced by n offspring of parents drawn with probability proportional to fitness.

  • moran(): overlapping generations. A generation is n birth-death events; at each event a random individual dies and is replaced by the offspring of two parents drawn with probability proportional to fitness (they can be the same individual, as in wright_fisher()). The offspring mutates with the model's per-generation rates, so the mutational input per generation is the same as with wright_fisher(). Drift per generation is about twice as strong as with wright_fisher() at the same n.

Usage

wright_fisher()

moran()

viability_selection(mates = 2, offspring_per_mate = 2)

Arguments

mates

number of males each female mates with.

offspring_per_mate

number of offspring per female and male.

Value

An evomod_life_cycle object, for evomod_model().

Details

  • viability_selection(): the life cycle of Jones, Arnold & Burger (2003, 2004, 2014). Half the population is female; each female mates with mates males drawn at random (males can mate many times) and has offspring_per_mate offspring with each. Zygotes mutate, survive with probability equal to their fitness (absolute, W(z) <= 1), and n adults are drawn at random from the survivors (if fewer than n survive, survivors are resampled to keep n). n must be even. With the defaults (2 mates, 2 offspring each), the effective population size is about n, as with wright_fisher().

Statistics are recorded, and directional or fluctuating optima move, between generations.

Examples

moran()
#> $type
#> [1] "moran"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "evomod_life_cycle"
